name: The majority voted in favour of keeping unchanged the usual [second reading motion](https://peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/), which is "*that the bill be read a second time*" (parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill). This question was put after Gorton MP [Brendan O'Connor](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/gorton/brendan_o'connor) (Labor) moved an amendment that would have removed all the words after 'that' and replaced them with other words (see below). ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House expresses concerns over deficiencies in the bill, including the:* > > *(1) lack of certainty that the measure will lower payment times;* > > *(2) light treatment of supply chain financing; and* > > *(3) ability for businesses to hide extremely long payment times to small businesses".*
